title.narrative: Recovery Support to Returnees in Iraq to Strengthen Socio-Economic Stabilization, including Improved Food Security

description.narrative: The proposed project aims to strengthen social stabilization and increase access to food security and livelihoods in Iraq through: (a) rehabilitation or reconstruction of 150 units of houses damaged by the conflict, (b) rehabilitation of essential public infrastructure such as water, sanitation and hygiene facilities (WASH sector) and public facilities including schools (education sector) and community health centers (health sector), (c) rehabilitation or construction of marketplaces serving the agricultural sector, and (d) delivery of vocational training for at least 200 returnees, including farmers as well as unemployed young men and women in conflict-affected areas to increase their chances to have adequate income and/or other resources to access food though skill-building on agriculture/farming and facilitation of the rebuilding of their livelihood. The project will be implemented in Sinjar/Western Ninewa, Ninewa Governorate, focusing on under-serviced rural areas, including Solagh village in Sinjar where Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) is currently implementing the project titled “Social Cohesion for Durable Solutions”. In addition, throughout the project will incorporate the following components for the purpose of supporting and achieving “durable solutions”: • Capacity development and awareness-raising in food security related activities in response to the negative impact on the degradation of the agricultural sector and food situation and also current drought in Iraq, including the surging prices of daily living expenses of basic foods, due to the war in Ukraine towards the most vulnerable returnees particularly on the above-mentioned activities of (c) and (d). • Synergies and integrated approach by linking UN-Habitat’s activities to other projects in Sinjar area supported by other donors or implemented by other organizations, in particular collaborating closely with the Sinjar Durable Solutions Area Based Coordination (ABC) Group formed by UN agencies, NGOs and donors operating in Sinjar for peace building. • Greener solutions and sustainability by utilising environmentally friendly products such as solar panels, solar pumps, water saving devices, passive designs and greener retrofitting of buildings, and raising awareness on climate change by utilizing national, regional, and global knowledge and experience of UN-Habitat. • Hygiene promotion and awareness raising on resource efficiency by utilizing best practices and lessons learned from the FY2020 project of “Emergency Support to Returnees in Iraq after the Outbreak of COVID-19” and other UN-Habitat-led projects in Iraq. • High visibility of the project both domestically and internationally in order to re-gain the world’s attention towards the plight of vulnerable returnees who should not be left behind.
